Privacy Policy

Last updated: August 21, 2026

Privacy Policy

Otian AI LLC ("Otian AI," "we," "us," or "our") makes Archie, a desktop app for building personal AI agents that run on your own computer, and offers guided sessions to help people set them up. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have.

It covers three things, and they are quite different from one another: the Archie app, this website, and our guided services. The app is where most people's questions are, so it comes first. A plain-English version of this section, listing the connections Archie makes and what each carries, is on our Trust page.

The Archie App

What the app sends to us

Archie's servers receive three things about you always, and two more only where they apply:

  • Your email address, so you can sign in. It is held in our account system (Google Firebase).
  • Whether you have a current plan, so the app can let you in. Payments are processed by Stripe; we never receive or store your card details.
  • Which paid add-ons you have bought. Each purchase creates a permanent record (the add-on, the amount, and the date) so that you can re-install what you have paid for. This means we know which paid add-ons you own. Installing a free add-on sends only a request to raise that add-on’s public install count; we keep no per-person record of which free add-ons you own.
  • Which version of Archie you are running, and a crash report if it breaks. Once every six hours the app records your account ID, its version number, whether you are on Mac or Windows, which edition it is, and the time. It overwrites the same record each time, and it exists so we know which versions are still in use before we ever stop supporting one. If Archie quits unexpectedly, the next time you open it a crash report goes with it: where in our code it happened and a shortened trace, scrubbed of anything secret-shaped. The crash message itself stays on your disk and is never uploaded. Neither one carries anything you wrote, received, or asked for, and there is no analytics service in Archie: nothing records what you do in it. Two counters do exist, and neither is analytics: the app keeps a log on your own computer of what each AI call cost, so its Account screen can show you your estimated spending, and while you are on the free starter credits our billing server counts what each call spent, because that is how the credits are subtracted. You can turn the version line and crash reports off, in the app under Settings, on a page that lists in full what is in each. Off means nothing further is sent and anything waiting to be sent is deleted.
  • The messages between your computer and your phone, if you turn on phone access. They sit in our database sealed with a key your computer generates and hands to your phone by QR scan. The key never reaches us, so we hold the messages and cannot read them. Phone access is off unless you switch it on, per computer.

Archie also checks our website for a new version. That request carries no version number, no device identifier, and no account information: it fetches a fixed file and the comparison happens on your computer. Our website is hosted on GitHub Pages, so GitHub's servers see the request's IP address and the usual request details; we run no server for this and receive no logs of it.

What stays on your computer

Your agent's instructions, the files and notes you give it, everything it remembers, and your entire conversation history are stored on your own device, in Archie's application folder. We do not receive, store, or have any means of accessing them. Two exceptions, both described in full elsewhere in this policy: while you are using the free credits Archie starts you with, your conversations pass through our server on the way to the AI (see Your AI provider below), and if you turn on phone access, a sealed copy that only your own key can open sits in our database (see the list above). One thing to know about deleting: dragging the app to the Trash does not remove that folder or your keys, because your computer keeps app data separate from apps. To erase everything, use the factory reset inside Archie, under Account, before you delete the app (on Windows, the uninstaller offers a box that does the same).

The app contains no analytics or tracking software of any kind: not disabled by default, but absent. Nothing in Archie records what you open, what you run, or how often you use it, and there is no third-party analytics service in it to do so. The two things it does send, the version line and the crash report, are described above and can be switched off.

Your AI provider

To think, your agent must send your request to an AI model. You choose the provider: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (ChatGPT), Google (Gemini), Groq, xAI (Grok), DeepSeek, Mistral, or any other provider of your own that speaks the OpenAI format. Archie connects directly from your computer to the one you chose, using your own account and your own API key. That traffic does not pass through us, is not relayed or proxied by us, and we keep no copy of it. It is governed by your agreement with that provider, not with us, and providers differ in ways that matter: where they run, how long they keep API traffic, and whether they train on it are their policies, not ours, so read the terms of the one you pick. If your agent searches the web, that search runs on the provider's infrastructure and is billed to your account.

The free credits are the exception. New installs come with a small amount of AI usage so you can try an agent before opening an account of your own. That usage runs on Claude, on an Anthropic account of ours, so those requests and their replies go to a server we operate, which forwards them to Anthropic and subtracts what they cost from what you were given. We do this because the alternative is putting our own provider key inside the app on your computer, where anyone could take it. That server does not log your request, the reply, or any part of either: what it records is your account ID, how many tokens went each way, and the amount spent. Connect an AI account of your own and this path stops being used from each agent's next start; the setup flow restarts your agent for you when you connect there, and an agent you leave running while adding a key in Settings switches over when it next starts.

Your API key is stored in your operating system's Keychain. It is transmitted only to the AI provider itself, and we have no means of reading it.

Accounts you connect

You may connect accounts you already use: Google (Gmail, Calendar and Tasks), Microsoft (Outlook mail and calendar, including Office 365), Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Todoist, Fireflies, GoHighLevel, and any other service you connect with a key of your own. Archie talks to those services directly from your computer, using access tokens issued to you and stored in your operating system's Keychain. The contents of those accounts are not sent to us, and we have no ability to access them. You can disconnect any of them at any time from within the app. iMessage, on a Mac, works differently, and it is worth reading the next section rather than this one.

Text messages, on a Mac

There is no account to connect for this. Archie reads and sends through the Messages app on the computer it runs on, under permissions you grant in macOS. What follows is what happens on your side of that, because one of these features reads messages other people wrote.

Using iMessage as the app you talk to your agent in. Your agent lives in your own message-yourself thread. It reads that one conversation and no other, and it can never reply to anybody else, because the only conversation it is bound to is the one with yourself. What you say there is your conversation with your agent, and it travels like any conversation with your agent: straight to your own AI account, or through our server while you are on the free starter credits, exactly as described under Your AI provider.

Text Replies, if you install it. This one reads the texts other people send you, so it can tell you which need an answer, offer a reply for you to send, and remind you of anything you agreed to. Because of that it deserves to be spelled out:

  • It never runs on the free starter credits. Those pass through our server, and the people who text you never agreed to that, so the feature refuses to start until your agent has an AI account of your own. No text handled by this feature ever touches a server of ours.
  • It reads texts as they arrive, only while your agent is running, and never trawls your history on its own. When a new text arrives, it also reads the last few messages of that one conversation (up to twelve, which can include messages from before you switched it on), so the reply it offers fits the thread.
  • Verification codes, texts from short-code senders, and messages carrying opt-out phrasing like "reply STOP" are dropped on your computer, before any AI reads them. Group chats are excluded unless you turn them on. So is anyone you put on its ignore list, and if you set it to watch only certain people, everybody else is dropped too. A message past those filters is judged by the AI, so ordinary promotional texts can reach it.
  • The text of a message leaves your computer in two ways. It goes to the AI account you connected, directly from your computer on your own key, so it can be read and answered; we are not in the middle of it and we keep no copy. And the card offering you the reply, which quotes the message, arrives through whatever chat app your agent uses, so it crosses that platform's servers the way anything you read there does.
  • It reads your address book, on your computer, to turn a phone number into the name you saved for it. The lookup itself never leaves the machine; the resolved name then appears on the card, in the request to your AI account, and in any reminder it sets, and nothing else about the contact goes anywhere.
  • If you switch it on, it also reads the messages you send, to catch things you promised. Off unless you ask for it.
  • Nothing is ever sent without you pressing Send. Every reply is a draft you read first and can rewrite. A reply you do send goes from your own number, in your own thread, exactly as if you had typed it, because iMessage has no way to mark a message as written by an assistant.
  • The text of your messages is never written into Archie’s logs. The internal draft record is deleted within a day; the card your agent posted stays in your chat like any message there, and a commitment it caught lives on as a reminder until it fires.
  • You can turn the whole thing off, or uninstall it, at any time in the app.

Google user data (Gmail, Calendar and Tasks)

When you connect Google, Archie asks only for the permissions you tick on the connect screen, plus one that comes with any connection: your email address, which is how the app shows you which account you connected. The rest are separate permissions, and one you do not tick is never requested:

  • Read your mail, so it can tell you what needs a reply and find what you ask it for.
  • Send a reply, which it only ever does after showing you the exact text and waiting for you to press Send.
  • File mail out of your inbox, which is a label change. It never deletes an email, and anything it files is still in All Mail.
  • See your calendar, so it can tell you what your week looks like and find you a free hour.
  • Change your calendar. Every change is proposed first and applied only after a later message from you; the AI is what reads your message as a go-ahead, and nothing applies while you are away.
  • Your Google Tasks, so it can add and complete items on your list.

This Google user data is handled under Google's rules for apps that use its APIs:

Archie's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements. Concretely, your Google data is:

  • used only to provide and improve the email, calendar and task features you see in the app, and for no other purpose;
  • fetched directly between your computer and Google: it is never stored on or accessible by Otian's servers. The starter-credits exception that applies everywhere in this policy reaches only your calendar and task data here: while you are on the free starter credits, what your agent reads there rides its AI requests through our server, unlogged, on the way to Anthropic (see Your AI provider). Your mail never rides them, because every email feature refuses to run on the starter credits and starts working when you connect an AI account of your own;
  • sent to the AI account you connected, and only so it can answer you. Reading an inbox means giving a model something to read, so the message text goes to the provider you connected, on your account and your key, directly from your computer. We are not in the middle of it and we keep no copy;
  • never used by us to train anything: we keep no copy that could be. Once sent to the AI provider you connected, training use is governed by your agreement with that provider;
  • never sold, and never transferred to anyone besides the AI account above and the places you point your agent's answers at: the chat app you connected (cards and answers about your mail are delivered as messages there) and, if you turn on phone access, the sealed relay only your key can open. Beyond those, only to comply with the law or in connection with a merger of which you are notified;
  • never read by a human except with your explicit consent (for example, to troubleshoot a problem you report to us), where required for security, or to comply with the law.

What Archie keeps on your computer between sessions: a marker of where it last read up to, so it does not re-read the same mail twice; each proposed reply (the sender, the subject, a one-line summary, and the draft text) for about a day, so the card's buttons keep working; fingerprints of replies it sent, so it can recognize its own writing later; and, only if you turn on the writing-style option, samples drawn from your sent mail, kept until you delete them. Message contents beyond that are read to answer you and are not stored, except whatever ends up in the conversation you can see and delete.

Microsoft account data (Outlook mail and calendar)

Outlook and Office 365 accounts work the same way and are treated the same way. When you connect one, Archie asks to know which account it is (sign-in identity, which every connection includes) and, beyond that, only for the permissions you tick on the connect screen: reading your mail, sending a reply, moving mail out of your inbox, seeing your calendar, and changing your calendar are separate permissions, and one you do not tick is never requested. Everything above about your Google data is equally true of your Microsoft data, including its exceptions: it is used only for the email and calendar features you can see, it moves directly between your computer and Microsoft, it is never stored on our servers (with the same starter-credits note as above), we never use it to train anything and once at your AI provider its use is governed by your agreement with them, and it is never sold. Access tokens are stored in your operating system's Keychain, and you can disconnect the account at any time from within the app, or revoke it yourself at myaccount.microsoft.com.

What your agent can and cannot do on its own

We think you should know this before you connect anything, so we state it plainly. Archie can send email, send a text reply, and change a calendar you connect, but never on its own: no email or text goes out until you press Send on the exact draft, and no calendar change applies on the turn it was proposed; only the exact proposed change can apply, never while you are away, and the AI is what reads your later message as the go-ahead. It has no purchase or payment feature, and nothing in it can spend money on its own; if you connect a payment service with a key that can move money, any change there is shown to you first and happens only after you approve it, and the app steers you toward read-only keys. On its own, your agent speaks only in the chats you connected, to the people on its list; the only way words it wrote reach anyone else is a draft (an email or a text reply) that you read and send yourself.

Review what it proposes before you approve it; an approval only protects you if you read it. The current status is always on our Trust page.

Our Website and Guided Services

The rest of this policy concerns our website and the guided sessions, calls, and communications that are part of our services, not the app.

Information We Collect

We collect information you choose to give us, including:

  • Contact and intake information, such as your name, email address, phone number, and the details you share in our contact form, intake questionnaire, or discovery call about what you'd like help with.
  • Session and communication records, such as notes from calls, emails, and messages we exchange while scoping and building your agent.
  • Billing information, such as the details needed to invoice you for guided sessions. We do not directly store full payment card numbers; payments are handled through the payment method we agree on with you.

We do not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics on this website. The outside resources our site does load are: Google Fonts, to display text in the site's typeface; Google's Firebase sign-in code and services, which power signing in and reading your own account; Formspree, which receives what you type into the contact form so it can reach us; and, on pages that offer booking, an embedded Google Calendar.

How We Use Your Information

We use the information we collect to:

  • Respond to inquiries and schedule consultations and sessions
  • Understand what you need help with and plan how to build it
  • Deliver, support, and maintain the AI agent we build with you
  • Send invoices and handle payment for our services
  • Improve how we explain and deliver our services

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it with third parties for their own marketing purposes.

Access to Your Accounts During Setup

Building your agent sometimes involves connecting it to accounts you already use, such as email or a calendar. We only ever connect or configure something after you've explicitly approved it during a guided session; nothing is set up behind the scenes. We do not retain copies of your account credentials once a session ends, and we do not access your connected accounts outside of scheduled sessions unless you've asked us to for support.

Third-Party AI Providers

The agents we build typically run on AI models from providers such as Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI (ChatGPT). You create and pay for your own account directly with the provider you choose. We do not resell or mark up that cost. Information you send to your agent (for example, an email draft it helps you write) is processed by that provider under their own privacy policy and terms, which we encourage you to review. We don't control, and aren't responsible for, how those providers handle data on their end.

Service Providers We Use

We rely on a small number of trusted companies ("subprocessors") to run our accounts, billing, and communications. Each processes only the limited information described above, only to provide its service to us, and under its own terms and security practices:

  • Google Firebase: sign-in and the account record (your email and license status).
  • Stripe: payment processing. Stripe handles your card details directly; we never receive or store them.
  • Resend: delivery of transactional email such as sign-in codes, verification, and account notices. Resend receives your email address in order to deliver these messages.
  • Render: hosting for the small service that handles sign-in, licensing, account management, and account email, and that relays your AI requests while you are on the free starter credits (forwarding them to Anthropic without logging their content).

We do not use third-party advertising or analytics services.

Data Retention

We keep intake, session, and billing records for as long as needed to provide our services and to meet our own recordkeeping and tax obligations, and we delete or anonymize them when they're no longer needed. You can ask us to delete your contact and intake information at any time; see "Your Choices" below.

Data Security

We take reasonable steps to protect the information you share with us, including limiting who has access to it. That said, no method of storage or transmission is completely secure, and we can't guarantee absolute security.

Children's Privacy

Our services are intended for adults. We don't knowingly collect information from anyone under 18.

Your Choices

You can ask us to access, correct, or delete the personal information we hold about you, or ask us to stop using it for a particular purpose, by emailing us at the address below. We'll respond as quickly as we reasonably can. You can also delete your account yourself from your account page (it asks you to have signed in recently first). That removes your sign-in, your account record, and your purchase history; a few operational records outlive it for the reasons they exist at all, including crash reports, the version line, and the free-credit ledger with its abuse-prevention counters, none of which contains anything you wrote. Email us to ask for those too.

Your Privacy Rights (GDPR & U.S. State Laws)

Depending on where you live, you may have rights over your personal information, including the right to access it, correct it, delete it, receive a portable copy, or object to or restrict certain uses. To exercise any of these, email us at the address below; we will not discriminate against you for doing so.

If you are in the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom, our lawful bases for processing your information are: performance of a contract (to provide the app, licensing, and services you buy), legitimate interests (to secure our systems and communicate with you about your account), and consent (for anything you optionally connect, such as your Google account, which you can withdraw at any time by disconnecting it in the app).

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, as those terms are defined under California and other U.S. state privacy laws.

Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time as our services change. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page reflects the most recent revision. If changes are significant, we'll do our best to let existing clients know directly.

Contact Us

Questions about this policy or your information? Email us at questions@otianai.com.
